body.name: Observed-law-preserving response-tree gluing handle
body.construction: Given an observed-data law with an admitted sustained-arm full-data extension and \(\gamma\in\mathcal G_H(p_{BT},q)\), \(\mathfrak L\) retains the original joint law of the raw intensive and standard sustained histories. For each intensive survivor with realized \((B,T)=(b,t)\) and \(p_{bt}>0\), it draws \(W=w\) with probability \(\gamma_{btw}/p_{bt}\), copies the intensive history through \(k\), keeps the otherwise unobserved switched branch alive through \(K\), and adds exactly \(w\) raw events immediately after \(k\). For histories dead by \(k\), it continues the absorbing path. It fills every other unused branch by copying the common prefix to its first treatment divergence and then appending zero-event legal histories, packages the table as \(U\), and draws \(R\) independently of that table. Conditional on \(R=a\), censoring is then drawn from the original sequential continuation kernel as a function of \(C\ge\ell-1\), \(D_{\ell-1}^a=0\), and \(\mathcal H_{\ell-1}^a\). Because the sustained histories and this factual-arm kernel are unchanged, the construction preserves the observed pushforward and the factual-arm sequential coarsening-at-random and positivity conditions without imposing any restriction between censoring and unassigned counterfactual branches. Zero-probability \((b,t)\) cells use arbitrary conditional values.
